big_idea: Building a successful business requires far less than conventional wisdom assumes: less planning, less staff, less funding, less bureaucracy. Small, fast, constraint-embracing teams that ship real work beat companies that plan and meet instead of build.

tool.label: Build half a product, not a half-assed product
tool.text: Instead of cramming in every feature before launch, cut scope ruthlessly and ship a smaller but fully realized core product, illustrated by the authors' own Basecamp launch, which shipped without billing functionality because it wasn't essential yet.
tool.note: One of several contrarian mantras in the book, alongside planning is guessing and embrace constraints, drawn directly from the authors' experience building 37signals and Basecamp.

ideas.title: Planning is guessing
ideas.text: Long-range business plans are speculation dressed up as strategy; the authors favor short, reversible decisions over rigid roadmaps.

ideas.title: Workaholism isn't dedication
ideas.text: Long hours signal a broken process, not commitment; overworked employees produce worse judgment and burn out teams around them.

ideas.title: Constraints breed creativity
ideas.text: Limited time, money, or people force sharper, simpler decisions instead of enabling bloat.

ideas.title: Meetings are costly by default
ideas.text: A one-hour meeting with ten people burns ten person-hours; most meetings lack a clear goal or outcome.

ideas.title: Write and market like a human
ideas.text: Marketing copy and communication should sound like talking to a friend, not corporate jargon; authenticity builds more trust than polish.

ideas.title: Take a stand
ideas.text: A product or company with a clear point of view and willingness to alienate some people differentiates better than one trying to please everyone.

try_it: Cancel or shorten one recurring meeting this week and replace it with a written update.
Pick one project you're over-planning and cut the plan down to what's the very next action, nothing further out.
Identify one extra feature or task you're adding out of habit and cut it, shipping the smaller, complete version instead.
Rewrite one piece of outward communication in plain, conversational language, as if writing to a friend.
best_for: People skeptical of corporate meeting and planning culture
less_useful: Readers at large, highly regulated organizations
Anyone seeking detailed financial or operational how-to rather than philosophy

related.why: A similar case for radical simplicity, focused on personal priorities rather than products
A complementary look at cutting the non-essential to protect what actually matters
